svg.title: How sync actually works
svg.desc: Nine connector concepts, each with its business effect: Modified-date watermark; Content hashing; Settled-record skip; Polling vs webhooks; Pagination that can't lie; REST vs GraphQL; Idempotent typed IDs; Backoff with jitter; Checkpoint after verified writes.
svg.text: The concepts behind every connector I ship.
Read only records with updated_at after
the last one seen, minus a small overlap for
smaller syncs, fresher data, lower API
No reliable timestamp? Hash the mapped
fields; send only on change. Cut ~1.3k
Stop re-fetching records already in a
shorter syncs and fewer API calls
Polling: I ask on a schedule, self-healing.
Webhooks: they tell me now, at-least-once,
Cursor or keyset beats offset; time
windows split when a page cap hits. A
page-100 cap once gave 5k of 88k orders.
REST: many endpoints, fixed shapes, N+1
calls. GraphQL: one exact nested query,
cost-based limits, errors that arrive with
Stable ids prefixed by type, so retries never
duplicate and order-123 never collides with
no duplicates or collisions, so reports
backoff plus jitter. Never retry a 4xx: that is
syncs survive rate limits without manual
Save state only after the upload is verified;
offload state past 8 MB to an artifact.
no lost or duplicated data after a crash
